intro: No jargon, no hype. Ten minutes here and you will know enough to start. Each answer starts with the short version.

cards.title: What is AI, really?
cards.answer: Today's AI tools are software trained on huge numbers of examples (text, images, audio) that produce new text, images or answers from the patterns they learned.
cards.body: They do not 'know' things the way a person does; they are very good at producing likely, useful-looking output. The free Elements of AI course points out that AI means different things to different people, so it helps to be specific: most people today mean chatbots like ChatGPT or Claude.

cards.title: What is a chatbot like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?
cards.answer: A chat app that sits on top of a 'model', the trained AI that actually writes the replies.
cards.body: You type or speak; the model answers. Companies release new models every few weeks, which is why the Latest models table below exists.

cards.title: Can AI be wrong?
cards.answer: Yes. AI can confidently invent facts, links or numbers that sound right.
cards.body: Treat it like a fast, clever intern: great for drafts and ideas, but check anything important yourself, especially health, money and legal questions. Ask it for links and open them.

cards.title: How do I write a good prompt?
cards.answer: Say who it should act as, what you want, who it is for and what format you need.
cards.body: Example: 'Act as a friendly tutor. Explain inflation to a 14-year-old in 5 bullet points.' Then reply with 'shorter', 'more examples' or 'now as a table'.

cards.title: Is it safe to paste personal information into a chatbot?
cards.answer: Don't paste passwords, bank details, medical records or other people's private information.
cards.body: Check each app's settings for whether your chats are used for training. Claude's pricing page, for example, lists model training as opt-out on its consumer plans.

cards.title: Do I need to pay to use AI?
cards.answer: No. ChatGPT and Claude both have free plans, with usage limits.
cards.body: ChatGPT's pricing page says the free version is available to everyone; Claude's Free plan is $0. Upgrade only when you keep hitting a limit doing something genuinely useful.

cards.title: Which AI chatbot should a beginner start with?
cards.answer: Start with the free plan of ChatGPT or Claude; both work on web and mobile.
cards.body: Both pricing pages list free chat on the web and phone apps, plus voice. Pick one, use it for a week on real tasks (an email, a plan, a summary), then try the other on the same task and compare.
